symptoms.symptom: Burners have yellow or yellow-tipped flames

causes.label: The combustion quality of burner flames needs to be determined visually.
remedies: Use the illustrations below to determine if your burner flames are normal.
If burner flames look like A, call for service.
Normal burner flames should look like B or C, depending on the type of gas you use.
With LP gas, some yellow tipping on outer cones is normal.
A–Yellow flames    B–Yellow tips        C–Soft blue flames Call for service   on outer cones       Normal for natural Normal for LP gas    gas
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "The combustion quality of burner flames needs to be determined visually."

causes.label: Controls improperly set.
remedies: To turn from the OFF position, push the knob in and then turn.

causes.label: Plug on cooktop is not completely inserted in the electrical outlet.
remedies: Make sure electrical plug is plugged into a live, properly grounded outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Plug on cooktop is not completely inserted in the electrical outlet."

causes.label: Gas supply not connected or turned on.
remedies: See the Installation Instructions that came with your cooktop.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Gas supply not connected or turned on."

causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: Igniter orifice in burner body may be clogged.
remedies: See the Care and cleaning of the cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Igniter orifice in burner body may be clogged."

causes.label: Burner parts not replaced correctly.
remedies: See the Care and cleaning of the cooktop section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Burner parts not replaced correctly."

causes.label: Hole in burner top behind the igniter may be clogged.
remedies: Use a small sewing needle to unplug.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Hole in burner top behind the igniter may be clogged."

symptoms.symptom: Ticking sound of spark igniter persists after burner lights

causes.label: Control knob is still in the LITE position.
remedies: Turn the knob out of the LITE position to the desired setting.
Turn the burner off and relight.
If ticking is still present, call for service.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Control knob is still in the LITE position."

symptoms.symptom: Burner flames very large or yellow

causes.label: Improper air to gas ratio.
remedies: If cooktop is connected to LP gas, check all steps in the Installation Instructions that came with your cooktop.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 13: "Improper air to gas ratio."
